In [[commutative algebra]], given a [[ring homomorphism|homomorphism]] <math>A\to B</math> of [[commutative ring]]s, <math>B</math> is called an <math>A</math>-[[associative algebra|algebra]] of '''finite type''' if <math>B</math> can be [[Finitely generated algebra|finitely generated]] as an <math>A</math>-[[algebra over a field#generalization: algebra over a ring|algebra]]. It is much stronger for <math>B</math> to be a '''finite''' <math>A</math>-algebra, which means that <math>B</math> is [[Finitely_generated_module|finitely generated]] as an <math>A</math>-[[module (mathematics)|module]]. For example, for any commutative ring <math>A</math> and natural number <math>n</math>, the [[polynomial ring]] <math>A[x_1,\dots,x_n]</math> is an <math>A</math>-algebra of finite type, but it is not a finite <math>A</math>-algebra unless <math>A</math> = 0 or <math>n</math> = 0. Another example of a finite-type homomorphism that is not finite is <math>\mathbb{C}[t] \to \mathbb{C}[t][x,y]/(y^2 - x^3 - t)</math>.

{{expert needed|Mathematics |talk=distinction between finite type and locally of finite type|date=August 2023}}

The analogous notion in terms of [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]]s is that a [[morphism of schemes|morphism]] <math>f:X\to Y</math> of schemes is of '''finite type''' if <math>Y</math> has a covering by [[affine scheme|affine]] [[open set|open]] subschemes <math>V_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)</math> such that <math>f^{-1}(V_i)</math> has a finite covering by affine open subschemes <math>U_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{ij})</math> of <math>X</math> with <math>B_{ij}</math> an <math>A_i</math>-algebra of finite type. One also says that <math>X</math> is of '''finite type''' over <math>Y</math>.

For example, for any natural number <math>n</math> and [[field (mathematics)|field]] <math>k</math>, [[affine space|affine <math>n</math>-space]] and [[projective space|projective <math>n</math>-space]] over <math>k</math> are of finite type over <math>k</math> (that is, over <math>\operatorname{Spec}(k)</math>), while they are not finite over <math>k</math> unless <math>n</math> = 0. More generally, any [[quasi-projective scheme]] over <math>k</math> is of finite type over <math>k</math>.

The [[Noether normalization lemma]] says, in geometric terms, that every affine scheme <math>X</math> of finite type over a field <math>k</math> has a [[finite morphism|finite]] surjective morphism to affine space <math>\mathbf{A}^n</math> over <math>k</math>, where <math>n</math> is the [[dimension of a scheme|dimension]] of <math>X</math>. Likewise, every [[projective scheme]] <math>X</math> over a field has a finite surjective morphism to [[projective space]] <math>\mathbf{P}^n</math>, where <math>n</math> is the dimension of <math>X</math>.
